audit_scope: All 488 current catch labels compared to retained source-reviewed memberships and allocations, including zeros. Saved source evidence reused; no new taxonomic research or scientific execution.

membership_summary.plain_language_rule: Explicit membership in the source group-definition table
Taxonomy and source members support an assumed candidate set
Generic group fit requires ecological interpretation
Related taxa extend the source-listed representatives
Documented generic group definition fits the catch taxon
Broad reporting category approximated across plausible groups
Source membership confirmed through an accepted synonym
Closest represented taxonomic or ecological analogue
Ecological assignment inferred from source habitat and size

allocation_summary.plain_language_rule: One group receives the entire taxon catch
Fixed 1985 source-model landings plus discards proportions

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Unlisted demersal/reef/estuarine bony fish connects to source large demersal predators21 or medium benthic feeders22 through source eel/salmon or mullet/wrasse/seabream members and provider habitat/size. Freshwater, tropical/reef, depth or trophic differences remain; no exact population represented.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Unlisted bony fishes are linked to source demersal predators or benthic feeders through named eel, salmon, mullet, wrasse or seabream analogues. Freshwater, reef, depth or feeding differences remain, and no exact population is represented.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Northeast Atlantic benthic fish connects to source25 gobies/blennies/dragonets through benthic habitat and small-body ecology; source22 is another benthic fish alternative. Provider large-reef classification is not a verified source cutoff; no exact source member and species/feeding differences remain.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Small benthic fish ecology connects these taxa to gobies, blennies and dragonets. The medium benthic feeder group is an alternative. No explicit source membership or verified source size cutoff resolves the species and feeding differences.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Unlisted deep demersal/benthopelagic fish connects to source21 via Helicolenus/Molva and22 via Phycis/Argentina. Source is shallow Celtic shelf; bathyal depth and unmeasured trophic composition mismatch. Dedicated hake/anglerfish guilds lack a positive taxon connection. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Deep demersal and benthopelagic fishes use Helicolenus/Molva and Phycis/Argentina analogues. The shallow Celtic shelf model does not resolve bathyal depth or trophic composition. Whole-guild source catch proportions determine the assumed split.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Deep demersal/benthopelagic bony fish connects to source21 via Helicolenus/Molva and22 via Phycis/Argentina. The provider pelagic/benthopelagic tag alone does not identify its feeding guild; both positive deeper-water fish analogues retained. Celtic shelf habitat, age, depth and diet differ. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Deeper-water analogues occur in both piscivorous and epibenthivorous demersal guilds. A pelagic or benthopelagic provider label does not resolve feeding membership. Depth, age, habitat and diet differences remain; source catch proportions supply the split.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Bathypelagic fish connects to mixed source24 through Maurolicus/Argentina and33 through offshore pelagic fishes. No dedicated deep-ocean guild exists; body size, depth and prey differ. Both positive analogues retained with uncertain mixture. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Maurolicus/Argentina and offshore pelagic fishes provide two weak analogues. No dedicated deep-ocean fish guild exists. Body size, depth and prey differ, and source catch proportions approximate the unknown mixture.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Unlisted deep demersal shark connects to source Squalus in piscivorous elasmobranch6. Source5 is mainly pelagic and7 benthic invertebrate-oriented; bathyal habitat, physiology and species diet differ from shelf Squalus.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Source Squalus provides a demersal shark connection, with poorer habitat or feeding matches in the other shark guilds. Bathyal habitat, physiology and species diets differ from the represented shelf population.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Pelagic large shark connection to named source sharks5. Basking shark is a filter feeder, unlike pooled piscivorous source members; zooplankton is prey, not a taxonomic shark compartment. No filter-feeding shark source exists.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: The pelagic shark group supplies the taxonomic and habitat connection, but basking shark is a filter feeder whereas the represented sharks are mainly piscivorous. No filter-feeding shark compartment exists.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Commercial benthic crab/lobster connects to source37 through named edible/spiny/clawed lobsters and large crabs. This unlisted species/family can differ in depth, body size and diet; small-crab/squat-lobster41 and Nephrops38 are distinct alternatives.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Named large crabs and lobsters support a commercial benthic crustacean analogue. These unlisted taxa differ in depth, size or diet. Small crabs, squat lobsters and Nephrops are distinct alternative compartments.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Benthic cartilaginous fish connects to source benthivorous rays/sharks7 through benthic prey and demersal habitat. Chimaeras are Holocephali, not source elasmobranch members; depth, physiology and diet composition differ. Piscivorous6 and pelagic5 are weaker habitat/feeding matches.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Demersal habitat and benthic prey connect chimaeras to benthivorous rays and sharks. Chimaeras are Holocephali, not elasmobranchs. Depth, physiology and diet differ, and no dedicated chimaera group is represented.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Chondrichthyes includes sharks, rays and chimaeras. Three source shark/ray guilds are eligible through actual sharks/rays; no explicit chimaera guild exists, so the chimaera component has only a benthic cartilaginous analogue. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Sharks and rays are represented across three source guilds, but chimaeras have only a weak benthic cartilaginous-fish analogue. The broad reporting mixture is unknown and is approximated by source guild catch proportions.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Unlisted demersal flatfish connects to source23 named benthivorous flatfishes through body form/benthic habitat. Source18/19/20 are named species and21 piscivorous turbot/halibut; target depth/feeding differs and no exact source member exists.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Benthic habitat and flatfish form connect this species to named endobenthivorous flatfishes. Other flatfish groups are species-specific or piscivorous. There is no exact source member, and depth and feeding differences remain.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Unlisted pelagic bony fish connects to source offshore tuna/pomfret33 or small/medium anchovy/shad/saury34 by pelagic habitat and provider size class. Named species-specific groups26–32 require membership evidence. Geography, prey and life stage differ.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Pelagic habitat and provider size class connect these unlisted fishes to offshore tuna/pomfret or smaller anchovy/shad/saury analogues. Geography, prey and life stage differ. Species-specific pelagic groups do not establish membership.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: WoRMS classifies this as freshwater, not marine. Source21 explicitly includes migratory eel/salmon and22 includes omnivorous mullets: a positive bony-fish/feeding analogue only. Permanent freshwater habitat, life history and diet differ; provider size/habitat tags do not establish marine membership.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: These freshwater fishes have only weak feeding analogues in source eel/salmon or mullet-containing groups. Permanent freshwater habitat, life history and diet differ; provider habitat or size labels do not establish marine membership.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Provider common name is crabs, shrimps and lobsters; represented benthic fishery decapods span commercial crustaceans37, Nephrops38, Shrimps40 and small crabs/squat lobsters41. This is a fishery interpretation of the actual common-name bridge, not an exhaustive Crustacea taxonomic exclusion. Krill46 and near-bed mysids44 are excluded from this chosen residual-fishery approximation; broad taxonomy and unidentified reporting composition remain uncertain. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: The provider common name supports a benthic crabs, shrimps and lobsters approximation. Excluding krill and near-bed mysids remains an assumed reporting boundary. Unknown composition is represented by whole-guild source catches.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Provider Elasmobranchii means sharks, rays and skates, excluding chimaeras. All three source elasmobranch guilds represent actual members, with unknown reporting mixture. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: The shark, ray and skate label excludes chimaeras and has members in all three elasmobranch guilds. Its actual reporting composition is unknown; fixed source catch proportions approximate that mixture.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Unlisted large pelagic shark connects taxonomically and by pelagic habitat to source named pelagic sharks5. Demersal6/7 are alternatives with poorer habitat match; species geography/diet/body-size differ.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Taxonomy and pelagic habitat connect these unlisted sharks to named pelagic shark members. Demersal groups fit less well. Species distributions, diets and body sizes differ from the source population.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Source41 explicitly contains whelks, providing a benthic gastropod connection. Generic sea snails also include herbivorous grazers absent from the model; source42/43 are particle/deposit feeders, not a grazer compartment.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Source whelks provide a benthic gastropod connection, but the broad sea-snail label also includes herbivorous grazers. No grazer guild exists, and particle/deposit feeders are not equivalent feeding compartments.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Benthic gastropod analogue: source41 explicitly includes whelks. Reported abalone/limpet/periwinkle grazers differ from its predators/scavengers; no herbivorous benthic guild exists. Surface/subsurface particle feeders42/43 are not a closer taxonomic connection.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Whelks provide a benthic gastropod analogue for abalone, limpets and periwinkles. These grazers differ from the source predators and scavengers. No herbivorous benthic guild exists; particle feeders are not a closer taxonomic match.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: This distinct label explicitly includes krill as well as lobsters/crabs/shrimps. Include source benthic decapods37/38/40/41, near-bed mysids44 and macrozooplankton46 through euphausiids. Source44/46 are genuine zero catches, not missing; broad whole-guild catches are a weak composition proxy. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: The label includes krill as well as benthic decapods and near-bed mysids. Zero source catches for planktonic candidates are genuine. Whole-guild source catches remain a weak proxy for the unknown taxonomic mixture.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Provider residual marine-fish labels are FAO ISSCAAP39/Osteichthyes, excluding dedicated shark/ray guilds. All locally represented bony-fish guilds remain eligible; unidentified species, sizes and habitats are unknown. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: These residual bony-fish labels encompass named and residual fish guilds while excluding dedicated shark/ray groups. Species, size and habitat composition are unknown. Whole-guild source catch proportions approximate the mixture.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: ISSCAAP39 bony groundfishes: source demersal groups8–25 plus Boarfish, benthopelagic Blue whiting and mixed Pelagic–Large through its explicitly named Sebastes member. Group names alone cannot exclude these members; the mixed whole-guild proxy is weak. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: The groundfish approximation includes demersal guilds, Boarfish, benthopelagic Blue whiting and the mixed pelagic group containing Sebastes. Mixed whole-guild catches do not measure the actual residual groundfish composition.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: ISSCAAP39 bony pelagic fishes: dedicated pelagic groups26–34 plus mixed group24 through Maurolicus/Gadiculus and its plankton/micronekton definition. Dedicated sharks are outside this reporting scope; mixed guild catches include nonpelagic members. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Pelagic bony-fish guilds and the mixed plankton/micronekton-feeding group contain eligible members. Dedicated sharks fall outside the reporting scope. Mixed source-guild catches also contain nonpelagic members, weakening the assumed composition.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Provider Other demersal invertebrates category supports a chosen demersal fishery approximation: benthic cephalopods36, shellfish37–40 and benthic feeders41–43. It does not prove exclusive Invertebrata/common-name/FAO taxonomy. Plankton44–49 is excluded as an unverified caught-stage population under this assumption; broad reporting scope and unrepresented components remain uncertain. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: The provider tag supports a demersal fishery approximation across cephalopods, shellfish and benthic feeders. It does not establish an exhaustive taxonomic boundary. Plankton exclusions and unrepresented components remain uncertain.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Positive source diadromous members: salmon/trout/eel21 and shads/smelt34. Freshwater life phases and omitted lamprey/sturgeon groups differ; no observed target population mixture. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Source salmon, trout, eel, shad and smelt provide positive diadromous connections. Freshwater phases and omitted lamprey or sturgeon populations differ. Source catch proportions approximate an unobserved target mixture.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Provider label includes squids/octopuses, clams and sea snails: source35/36, commercial bivalves39 and explicit whelks41 are positive members; surface-deposit bivalves can connect to42. Herbivorous gastropods lack a dedicated source guild; broad mixed catches are uncertain. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Source cephalopods, bivalves and whelks provide represented molluscan members. Herbivorous gastropods lack a dedicated group. Unknown composition and mixed whole-guild catches make the allocation a weak approximation.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Lanternfish has a positive small offshore plankton/micronekton fish connection to source24 through explicitly listed Maurolicus. Named shelf small pelagics29/31/32/34 are alternatives but lack this offshore mesopelagic connection; depth/species/source geography differ.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Listed Maurolicus supports a small offshore plankton/micronekton-fish analogue. Named shelf small-pelagic groups offer a poorer mesopelagic connection. Depth, species and geographic differences remain.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Source36 explicitly contains benthic octopuses but reported Octopoda also covers pelagic argonauts; source squid35 is another cephalopod yet not an octopus member. Habitat/stage mixture is unidentified.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: The source group explicitly contains benthic octopuses, while the reported order also includes pelagic argonauts. The habitat and life-stage mixture is unidentified; a squid compartment does not establish octopus membership.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Unlisted small demersal/reef fish connects to named small benthic fishes25 (gobies/dragonets/blennies) by habitat/body-size; source22 has medium benthic feeders. Reef/depth/geographic and diet differences remain.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Small benthic habitat and body size connect these unlisted taxa to gobies, dragonets and blennies. Medium benthic feeders offer an alternative. Reef, depth, geography and diet differences remain.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: FNAM/WoRMS identifies a benthic shelf/slope roughshark, not a pelagic guild member. Source6 contains Squalus (same order Squaliformes),7 contains benthic sharks; retain both positive demersal shark connections because feeding composition is not established. Depth and species differ; no exact roughshark source exists. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Shelf/slope roughsharks connect to source Squalus and benthic sharks. Their feeding composition does not resolve the two demersal guilds. No exact roughshark member exists; source catches supply an assumed split.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Historical provider higher taxon spans source members now assigned to several modern orders. Eligible source guilds retain actual named perch-like/scorpionfish/tuna-mackerel members; modern rank alone cannot determine reporting composition. Whole mixed-guild proportions are weak. Allocation uses complete accepted 1985 source landings + discards by eligible guild, including true zeros; applied to 1950–2019 whole-LME landings/catch/discards as a fixed assumption. No compatible caught-mass stage/species composition found in bounded primary-source review.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Historical reporting names include source members now placed in several modern orders. Modern taxonomy alone cannot resolve the reported composition. Proportions of entire mixed source guilds are a weak proxy.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Migratory lamprey connects to source21 diadromous eel/salmon through migration and animal feeding; jawless parasitic life history and freshwater phases differ. No lamprey guild or exact taxon member exists.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Migration and animal feeding connect lampreys to source eel and salmon. Their jawless parasitic life history and freshwater phases differ. No lamprey guild or exact source member exists.

very_low_decisions.why_confidence_is_very_low: Benthic shrimp-like source40 connects morphologically/habitat to mantis shrimp. Target Stomatopoda differs from true decapod shrimp; source41 predators/scavengers is an alternative ecological guild but lacks a named stomatopod connection.
very_low_decisions.word_reason: Benthic shrimp-like form and habitat connect mantis shrimps to the shrimp group. Stomatopods differ from true decapod shrimps. The predator/scavenger guild is an alternative but has no named stomatopod connection.
